title: Add drift-aware tfstate snapshotter and eviction network-policy for GPU node pools
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a tfstate snapshotter with drift detection and retention; Add network-policy and eviction coordination for GPU node pools; New IAM role for snapshot service; Migration helper script for existing tfstate backends; Backward-compatible by default
description: Motivation: Private deployments observed hard-to-debug tfstate corruption and drift during long-running on-prem upgrades and intermittent network partitions. This PR adds a drift-aware tfstate snapshotter (as an optional terraform module) plus a Kubernetes network-policy + eviction coordination pattern to reduce unsafe in-place changes to GPU node pools during upgrades. Summary of changes: 1) terraform/modules/tfstate-snapshotter: new module that periodically takes consistent, encrypted snapshots of remote state backends (S3/GCS) and records metadata (sha256, apply-id, timestamp) for drift detection; supports kms_key and snapshot_prefix options. 2) terraform/modules/gpu-eviction-policy: network-policy and daemonset wiring to enforce a two-step eviction (cordon -> drain with soft-kill annotation) for GPU nodes during upgrades and autoscaling; includes safe drain hooks for long-running KV/caching workloads. 3) iam/roles.tf: new iam role 'tfstate-snapshotter' with minimal perms (GetObject/PutObject/List on snapshot prefix, kms:Encrypt/Decrypt as optional). 4) tooling: tools/tfstate-migrate-snapshots.sh to copy and backfill snapshots from existing buckets and to produce a mapping file for rollback. 5) helm/values.yaml bump for tfstate-exporter image and a new chart values entry to enable the eviction-daemonset. Backwards compatibility: the snapshotter is opt-in and disabled by default. Network policy changes are additive and gated by a feature flag in the installer config. Migration notes and example invocations are in migration_steps. Why this approach: separate, immutable snapshots provide fast recovery and a clear chain-of-evidence for apply-induced drift while the eviction pattern reduces pod loss and KV cache stomping when nodes are being recycled. The PR intentionally avoids changing the canonical tfstate layout; instead it layers snapshots and a small metadata index. Testing: unit tests for terraform module inputs, integration smoke tests in the benchmark-lab (single-region on-prem sim), and end-to-end upgrade run in a staging private cluster (logs attached). See files changed for details.
commits: 3 commits: (1) add tfstate snapshotter module + docs; (2) add gpu-eviction-policy module, daemonset and helm flag; (3) iam role and migration script + tests
review_comments: Omar Patel: Nice separation of concerns. A few nit picks -- can we reduce the default retention to 7 days and make TTL configurable? Also please add an acceptance test that simulates a partial upload failure.
Maya Chen (author): Updated retention default to 7 days and added --simulate-partial-upload flag in tests. See latest commit where smoke test covers a failed multipart upload scenario.

Jules Martín: The eviction flow looks good, but we need a safe-default to avoid interfering with low-latency inference services. Added request: set eviction gracePeriod to 5m and expose installer flag to disable eviction for labeled clusters.
Maya Chen (author): Applied change; gracePeriod default = 5m and feature flag installer.enable_gpu_eviction=false added. Documented behavior in README.
Priya Desai: IAM role looks principle-of-least-privilege, but request to add CloudTrail read permissions to help audits. Optional; added as separate variable to enable in highly-regulated installs.
Maya Chen (author): Added root-level var allow_audit_read and documented when to enable. CI green after fixes. Approved by reviewers.
testing_summary: Ran terraform plan/apply in isolated staging cluster with S3 backend and simulated network partitions; verified snapshots created and metadata sha256 matched applied tfstate; simulated node drains with eviction-daemonset and verified graceful KV cache rebuilds; migration script tested against snapshot bucket with 120 historical state files.
migration_steps: 1) opt-in: set installer.tfstate.snapshotter.enabled=true and provide snapshotter.s3.bucket and kms_key. 2) run tools/tfstate-migrate-snapshots.sh --source-bucket existing-backend --dest-prefix snapshots/<cluster> to backfill index. 3) verify index file generated at s3://<bucket>/snapshots/<cluster>/index.json and run terraform plan. Example: ./tools/tfstate-migrate-snapshots.sh --src s3://redwood-terraform-backend --dst s3://redwood-snapshots --prefix prod-cluster --dry-run
rollback_plan: If a regression is observed: 1) disable installer flag installer.tfstate.snapshotter.enabled=false and installer.enable_gpu_eviction=false and re-run a safe apply to revert daemonset changes; 2) restore tfstate from the most recent snapshot by using tools/tfstate-restore.sh (copies snapshot into backend path atomically); 3) if IAM role changes are problematic, revoke assume-role binding and re-apply previous IAM module commit. The snapshots are immutable and retained for configured TTL to facilitate fast rollback.
notes: Opt-in safety-first change. Ops runbook and runbook playbooks updated under docs/private-installer. No default behavior change for existing customers.
security_considerations: Snapshots are encrypted using provided KMS key; IAM role has narrow S3 prefix perms. Recommend customers rotate kms_key and review snapshot retention policy for regulatory needs.
operational_impact: Minor: new component (snapshotter daemon) may increase S3 requests and KMS usage depending on retention and frequency; default frequency set to 6 hours and retention to 7 days to keep costs low.
